sn12.31:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Savatthī.…
sn12.31:1.2: There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Sāriputta thus:
sn12.31:1.3: “Sāriputta, in ‘The Questions of Ajita’ of the Parayana it is said:
sn12.31:2.3: Asked about their way of conduct,
sn12.31:2.4: Being discreet, tell me, dear sir.’
sn12.31:3.1: How should the meaning of this, stated in brief, be understood in detail?”
sn12.31:3.2: When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta was silent.
sn12.31:4.1: A second time and a third time the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Sāriputta thus:
sn12.31:4.4: “Sāriputta, in ‘The Questions of Ajita’ in the Parayana it is said …
sn12.31:6.1: How should the meaning of this, stated in brief, be understood in detail?”
sn12.31:6.2: A second time and a third time the Venerable Sāriputta was silent.
sn12.31:7.1: “Sāriputta, do you see: ‘This has come to be’? Sāriputta, do you see: ‘This has come to be’?”
sn12.31:7.2: “Venerable sir, one sees as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This has come to be.’ Having seen as it really is with correct wisdom:
sn12.31:7.3: ‘This has come to be,’ one is practising for the purpose of revulsion towards what has come to be, for its fading away and cessation.
sn12.31:7.4: One sees as it really is with correct wisdom:
sn12.31:7.5: ‘Its origination occurs with that as nutriment.’ Having seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘Its origination occurs with that as nutriment, ’ one is practising for the purpose of revulsion towards its origination through nutriment, for its fading away and cessation.
sn12.31:7.6: One sees as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation.’ Having seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation,
sn12.31:7.7: ’ one is practising for the purpose of revulsion towards what is subject to cessation, for its fading away and cessation.
sn12.31:7.8: It is in such a way that one is a trainee.
sn12.31:8.1: “And how, venerable sir, has one comprehended the Dhamma?
sn12.31:8.2: Venerable sir, one sees as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This has come to be.’ Having seen as it really is with correct wisdom:
sn12.31:8.3: ‘This has come to be,’ through revulsion towards what has come to be, through its fading away and cessation, one is liberated by nonclinging.
sn12.31:8.4: One sees as it really is with correct wisdom:
sn12.31:8.5: ‘Its origination occurs with that as nutriment.’ Having seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘Its origination occurs with that as nutriment,’ through revulsion towards its origination through nutriment, through its fading away and cessation, one is liberated by nonclinging.
sn12.31:8.6: One sees as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation.’ Having seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘With the cessation of that nutriment, what has come to be is subject to cessation,’
sn12.31:8.7: through revulsion towards what is subject to cessation, through its fading away and cessation, one is liberated by nonclinging.
sn12.31:8.8: It is in such a way that one has comprehended the Dhamma.
sn12.31:8.9: “Thus, venerable sir, when it is said in ‘The Questions of Ajita’ of the Parayana:
sn12.31:9.3: Asked about their way of conduct,
sn12.31:10.1: dear sir.’— it is in such a way that I understand in detail the meaning of this that was stated in brief.”
sn12.31:11.1: “Good, good, Sāriputta!… the Buddha repeats here the entire statement of the Venerable Sāriputta …
sn12.31:14.1: it is in such a way that the meaning of this, stated in brief, should be understood in detail.”
